readme: WHICH FDC ENTRY IS THIS FOOD - the one call in the rung-2 backfill that a machine may not make. fdc_lookup's doctrine measured identity assertions at 37% false locally, and the first mechanical pass proved it live: the top CORROBORATING candidate for 'Bread Crumbs' was Croutons, for 'Rice' it was rice cakes, for 'Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh' it was chicken BREAST, and for 'Peanuts' it was a candy bar. Every one of those agreed inside tolerance. So agreement is necessary and not sufficient, and this file is the frontier ruling that goes with it: nothing is written to `source` unless it is named here AND the numbers still corroborate. Reviewed against the full curated shelf for all 98 Class A rows, 2026-08-26. Class B rulings added 2026-08-26 against FDC BRANDED shelves - rung 2 of the plan's ladder, the sanctioned fallback for a label that could not be photographed. A ruling must set `branded: true` to admit that tier at all: for a generic whole food a retail label is a weak answer, and for a manufactured product it IS the food.

Bread Crumbs.why: the top corroborating candidate was Croutons; this is the actual dry grated crumb entry

Cottage Cheese.why: the shelf's top agreeing rows were cottage cheese WITH VEGETABLES and WITH FRUIT; the stored 88 cal / 11.5 P per 100 g is the 2% milkfat entry

Cucumber.why: the row's own note says with peel, so the peeled entry is the wrong one

Frozen Chopped Spinach.why: unprepared, which is what the recipes weigh

Grits.why: the row is Quaker QUICK grits; the top hit was Quaker INSTANT

Olive Oil.why: the top corroborating candidate was a corn/peanut/olive BLEND

Pasta Shells.why: the shelf for 'shells' returns TOSTADA and TACO shells; this is the dry pasta entry the other pasta rows use

Pasta Shells - jumbo.why: same as Pasta Shells - the shelf returns taco shells

Shredded Carrots.why: shredded is a cut, not a different food

Spaghetti.why: the top corroborating candidate was SPINACH spaghetti

Sugar.why: the top corroborating candidate was turbinado

Toasted Sesame Seeds.why: roasted and toasted, which is what the row's name says

Zucchini.why: includes skin, raw - the top hit was BABY zucchini

Greek Yogurt.why: plain nonfat; the top hit was CHOBANI BLUEBERRY

Worcestershire Sauce.why: Kraft Heinz is Lea & Perrins' owner; 100 vs the stored 88 cal per 100 g is inside tolerance

Traditional Pasta Sauce.why: no Great Value entry; this store-brand traditional sauce reproduces the row exactly

Diced Tomatoes & Green Chilies.why: the row is already a Ro-Tel-style stand-in; this is another

Peanut Butter.why: the row is generic; this is one real label that reproduces it

Lo Mein Noodles.why: no Simply Asia lo mein entry; this one reproduces the row

Rotini Pasta.why: Barilla's own rotini entry is the REGULAR line at 321 cal / 14.3 g protein and the row is Protein Plus; this high-protein rotini reproduces the row

BBQ Sauce.why: the row is generic; this is one real label that reproduces it

Fajita Seasoning.why: no Taco Bell seasoning entry; this reproduces the row

Hot Honey.why: no Better Goods entry; three unrelated hot honeys all read 286/81, which is the row
